translations.text: Because of the sins you have committed before God, you will be taken as captives to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon.
When you enter Babylon, you will spend many years there, a long time, up to seven generations. After this, I will bring you out of that place in peace.
Now you will see in Babylon gods of silver, gold, and wood, which people carry upon themselves and which inspire fear among the nations.
So take care not to follow the example of the nations by fearing them, and do not let fear of them seize you.
When you see a crowd in front of them and following behind them, worshiping them, say in your hearts, “You alone, Lord, are the one who should be worshiped.”
For my angel will be with you; he is the one who will watch over your souls.
For a carpenter carved the tongues of their gods. Though they are covered with gold and silver, they are false and cannot speak.
And, as though for a young woman who loves adornment, they take gold
and make crowns, placing them on the heads of their gods. Sometimes the priests also take the gold and silver from their gods and divert it to themselves.
They also give some of it to the prostitutes at the brothel. They dress their gods in clothes like human beings, although they are gods of silver, gold, and wood.
These cannot rid themselves of tarnish and moths, even though people clothe them in purple garments.
People wipe their faces because of the dust of the house that has settled thickly upon them.
And you will find a golden staff in their hands, like a person who is a judge of a country, but they cannot kill those who sin against them.
They are also found with a sword in their right hand and an axe, but they cannot save themselves from war or robbers. This makes it clear that they are not gods. Do not fear them.
For just as a person's vessel, once it is broken, is no longer useful for anything,
This is what their gods are like: while they stand in their houses, their eyes fill with dust that rises onto them from the feet of those who come in to them.
and just as a person who has offended a king secures his dwellings because he fears death, so the priests secure their houses with doors, locks, and bolts, so that robbers will not plunder them.
People light many lamps for their gods, more than they light for themselves, but the gods cannot see any of them.
They are like a beam belonging to those who live in a house. Their insides are eaten away, as people say, while the creeping creatures of the earth eat them and their clothes, and they feel nothing.
Even when their faces turn black from the smoke in the house,
bats, swallows, birds, and cats settle on their bodies and their heads.
From this you will understand that they are not gods. So do not fear them.
For the gold with which they are covered to beautify them does not make them beautiful unless its tarnish is wiped away. For when they are cast, they feel nothing.
They have been bought at any price, although there is no spirit in them.
When people bring them out, they carry them on their shoulders because they have no feet with which to walk, exposing their disgrace to everyone. Those who serve them are ashamed,

lest they fall from their hands to the ground, for they cannot get up by themselves. Even if someone sets them upright, they cannot move by themselves. If they tilt over and fall, they cannot straighten themselves. Instead, people place gifts before them as they do before the dead.
The priests divide their sacrifices among themselves. Likewise, their wives salt some of them and give none of them to anyone poor or weak.
They are defiled by mothers who menstruate and by women in childbirth. Since you have understood from these things that they are not gods, do not fear them.
For how can they be called gods, when women set aside for themselves the sacrifices offered to their gods of silver, gold, and wood?
Their priests sit inside their houses with their clothes torn, their heads and beards shaved, and their heads uncovered.
They cry out before their gods like people taking part in a funeral ceremony.
The priests take some of their gods' clothes and put them on their wives and children.
And if someone does them either harm or good, they cannot repay him. Nor can they appoint a king or remove him.
Likewise, they cannot give wealth or money. And if someone makes a vow to them but does not fulfill it, they do not pursue him.
Nor can they rescue anyone from the power of death. They cannot deliver a poor person from the power of someone who oppresses him.
They cannot make a blind person see, and they cannot help someone in distress.
They cannot have mercy on a widow, nor can they do any good for an orphan.
Their gods of wood, gold, and silver are like stones taken from the mountain. Therefore, those who worship them will be put to shame because of them.
How, then, can they be regarded or called gods?
The Chaldeans themselves also dishonor them. If a deaf person who cannot speak comes before them, they appeal to Bel, crying out to him to heal them, saying that he has the power to perceive.
He does not perceive, and they go away and leave them, for there is no perception in them.
The women tie cords around themselves and sit along the roads, presenting offerings of bran that they have burned.
If one of the passersby draws one of them aside and sleeps with her, she taunts her companion because she was not chosen as she herself was, and the cord tied around her was not broken.
There is no truth in anything done for them. How, then, can they be spoken of, or even regarded, as gods?
Carpenters and goldsmiths made them, and nothing will come of them except what the craftsmen want.
Those who make them do not themselves live to a great age.
So how will the things they have made endure? For they are works of falsehood and objects of reproach left for those who come after.
For if war and disasters come upon them, the priests consult one another about where they can hide themselves along with them.
Why, then, do you not recognize that they are not gods, since they cannot save anyone, or others, from war or suffering?

For they are pieces of wood, gold, and silver. After these things, the nations will recognize that they are frauds. It will also become clear to kings that they are not gods but things made by human hands, with nothing divine in them.
Who, then, will fail to understand that they are not gods?
For they cannot establish a king over a country, nor can they give rain to people.
Nor can they decide a legal case or remove an injustice, for they have no power.

For they are like crows between heaven and earth. Indeed, if a fire breaks out in the house of gods of wood, gold, and silver, their priests run outside and escape, but their gods will be caught and burned like roof beams.
They cannot withstand a king or those who fight alongside him.
How, then, can they be spoken of, or even regarded, as gods? Nor can these gods of wood, silver, and gold save themselves from thieves and robbers.
Those who overpower them will strip them of their gold, silver, and clothing and walk away carrying them, and they will be unable to help themselves.

A man who shows his strength is therefore better than these false gods, as is a useful household object that its owner needs. A door in a house that protects what is inside will also be valued more than these false gods. And a wooden pillar in a palace is better than these false gods.

For the sun, the moon, and the stars are lights. When their creator sends them to perform their task, they obey him. The rainbow, too, appears beautifully whenever it appears. Yet the same wind blows in every land.
And whenever God commands the clouds to spread over the whole inhabited world, they carry out the task he has commanded them to do.

Likewise, whenever fire is sent out from heaven to burn the mountains and the wooded places, it performs the task it has been commanded to do. These, however, cannot compare with them, nor do they match them in appearance or strength.
Therefore, it is not right even to think of them as gods or to call them gods, since they cannot judge a case or do good to people.
Since you have therefore understood that they are not gods, do not be afraid of them.
For they cannot curse kings, nor can they bless them.
Nor can they show the nations signs in heaven. They cannot shine like the sun or give light like the moon.
Wild animals are better than they are: they run to shelter and gain some benefit for themselves.
It is clear to us that they are not gods in any way. Therefore, do not be afraid of them.
For their gods are like a scarecrow in a cucumber patch that protects nothing. They are wood, gold, and silver.
Their gods are also like a thornbush in a garden on which every bird perches, or like a dead person thrown into the darkness. They are wood, gold, and silver.

From the purple cloth that frays and the [?] that decays upon them, you will therefore understand that they are not gods. They themselves will be eaten away, and afterward they will become a disgrace in the land.
A righteous person is therefore better—a righteous person who has no idol—for he will be far from disgrace.
